text:
lisa (Support): Hi @customer-acme — we're tracking your SSE disconnects, thanks for the repro steps. Can you confirm this is Dedicated in a private VPC behind your corporate proxy?
customer-acme: yes — Dedicated pool in our VPC, on-prem egress through a corporate F5 + TLS-inspect proxy. We see streaming cut mid-chunk and client retries which sometimes create duplicate billing events.
lisa (Support): Got it. First-pass hypothesis: proxy/TLS-inspect or MTU-related fragmentation causing partial chunk delivery + client reconnect. Any recent change to MTU or proxy config?
customer-acme: nothing intentional. We do have a recent HAProxy->F5 change last week, but ops says no config changes.
tom (Eng): Could be the proxy splitting TLS records or reassembling in a way that breaks server-sent events framing. If the X-Accel/Transfer chunk boundaries get altered, clients see partial data and reconnect. Do you have a pcap or curl trace?
customer-acme: attaching a short tcpdump from client side (sent privately) and our app log: 
```
-> recv 0x1e bytes (partial payload)
-> keepalive timeout 10s
client reconnect, resume token present
```
alex (SRE): I see frequent TCP retransmits and occasional CWR on the capture. Also a stream where TLS inspector inserts close_notify mid-stream -> weird. That lines up with partial chunking.
infra-bot: incident-1234 created (priority: p2) — assigned to eng/sre/support.
tom (Eng): Repro plan: 1) run curl --http1.1 -v --no-buffer to our endpoint from inside the corp network to replicate; 2) capture server-side tls session id and seq; 3) try toggling proxy TLS-inspect bypass for the stream path.
lisa (Support): Customer, can you run this from a machine behind the proxy and paste output?
```
curl -v --http1.1 --no-buffer "https://api.redwood.example/v2/stream?model=redwood-large" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream"
```
customer-acme: ran it — output shows the SSE headers, then a ~1200-byte chunk, then silence and curl exits with "Connection reset by peer".
tom (Eng): Interesting — the ~1200 bytes matches one MTU-sized fragment plus some overhead. On some paths TLS inspect will re-chunk or close the TLS record after a threshold. That can break streaming framing if client expects continuous chunked encoding.
alex (SRE): Short-term mitigation options: 1) enable TCP keepalive and lower the SSE heartbeat interval (server-side) so clients treat silence as expected; 2) force smaller server chunk sizes so proxy doesn't hit its internal threshold; 3) ask proxy team to disable TLS-inspect for the /v2/stream path.
customer-acme: Can you suggest exact server-side flags? We don't control the corporate proxy.
tom (Eng): On our side we can lower server chunk to 512 bytes for this customer and add periodic 1s keepalive SSE comment lines (":\n") to keep the connection alive. We'll also add a temporary fallback route to Dedicated-tier non-inspected egress if available.
lisa (Support): I'll open a billing ticket to check duplicate-token events tied to reconnects — please include trace-id from customer logs.
customer-acme: trace-id 8f3b7c22-0a included in the logs. Thanks.
alex (SRE): One more ask: can you collect a server-side TLS session log around that trace-id and share the TLS record sizes (client_hello/server_hello/records)? We want to confirm the inspector is cutting records.
customer-acme: will do, sending privately now.
tom (Eng): Thanks — if TLS inspector is confirmed, recommended permanent fix is to either bypass inspect for streaming endpoints or enable HTTP/2 multiplexing with ALPN sticky sessions (proxy-dependent). But bypass is faster.
lisa (Support): Action items: 
- tom: deploy 512B chunk/1s keepalive change to try route (canary) — ETA 2h
- alex: correlate tcpdump + server tls record sizes for trace-id — ETA 3h
- support: billing ticket for duplicate events — assigned
- customer: provide server-side TLS logs and confirm when you can test bypass with proxy team
customer-acme: we're looping in proxy ops, will try bypass for /v2/stream on staging first.

lisa (Support): I'll follow up in 3h with status. :thumbsup:
